Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) of the province of the registered office, supervised by the Ministry of Justice; the Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) issues the negative name certificate only.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Capital Companies Act, Ley de Sociedades de Capital - LSC), specifically Articles 19-25 (formation deed and Mercantile Registry registration), Article 62 (minimum SL capital of EUR 3,000), Article 63 (full paid-up requirement upon incorporation), and Articles 209-215 (appointment of administrators); supplemented by the Mercantile Registry Regulation (Real Decreto 1784/1996) and Law 14/2013 on simplified incoror of the Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva.

Formation / constitutional filings

Public Deed of Incorporation (Escritura Pública de Constitución), which must be registered as the constitutive inscription (inscripción constitutiva) in the Mercantile Registry.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 20 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

For an SL, minimum share capital is EUR 3,000 (Article 62 LSC); 100% of the subscribed capital must be fully paid up in cash at incorporation (Article 63 LSC). The funds must be deposited into a temporary restricted bank account in Spain and evidenced by a bank certificate; after registration the administrators may freely use the funds for the corporate purpose.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety compliance under the Technical Building Code (CTE DB-SI) and the Fire Safety Installations Regulation (RIPCI), including fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, signage and evacuation routes, with certification by an authorized control body; municipal first-occupancy certificate (licencia de primera ocupación) verifying structural load safety; and approval of the Occupational Risk Prevention Plan under Law 31/1995, including the workplace risk assessment, electrical installation inspection and employee health surveillance.

Paid-in capital rule: For an SL, minimum share capital is EUR 3,000 (Article 62 LSC); 100% of the subscribed capital must be fully paid up in cash at incorporation (Article 63 LSC). The funds must be deposited into a temporary restricted bank account in Spain and evidenced by a bank certificate; after registration the administrators may freely use the funds for the corporate purpose.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [MCN COMPANY], S.L.
The undersigned sole shareholder hereby RESOLVES:
1. Ratifying the incorporation deed executed before the Notary on [date];
2. Accepting the full subscription and paid-up capital of EUR 3,000.00, divided into 3,000 participaciones of EUR 1.00 each, credited by bank deposit certificate;
3. Adopting the registered office at [address], Madrid, Spain;
4. Appointing [Name, Passport No.] as sole Administrator (Administrador Único) for an indefinite term with full powers of management, representation and control;
5. Authorizing the Administrator to complete Mercantile Registry registration, obtain the definitive NIF, open bank accounts, and procure all permits necessary to commence operations.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Exempted / Not Required

Municipal Directorate for Urban Planning and Licensing (e.g., Área de Licencias y Urbanismo, Ayuntamiento de Madrid), handling the administrative communication for office and light service premises of Class I activity

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es).

E-government filing portal

For the newly incorporated SL with non-resident shareholders: (1) Before deed execution, the promoters apply for a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) by filing Form 036 (Declaración Censal) at the local AEAT office, either in person or through the notary; the intended legal representative is named as the contact person. (2) Execute the public deed of incorporation before a Spanish notary and, within the legal term, inscribe the SL in the provincial Registro Mercantil. (3) After the Mercantile Registry certificate of inscription is issued, file a second Form 036 to convert the provisional NIF into the definitive NIF; AEAT issues the definitive NIF certificate electronically. (4) Simultaneously register the economic activity (IAE epigraph Group 731 – Advertising/Publicidad if applicable) and, if any physical merchandise export will occur, apply for the Código EORI, which is linked to the definitive NIF and issued by the AEAT customs office. (5) Configure the AEAT digital certificate (certificado electrónico) and Cl@ve PIN for the legal representative to make all recurring filings (VAT Models 303/390; Corporate Income Tax Model 200; withholding Models 111, 115, 123). (6) Where a non-EU shareholder holds 10% or more, complete the statistical registration with the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores (Law 19/2003 and Law 18/2022); this is not a tax precondition but a completeness requirement. No additional tax license or pre-clearance is required to start operations; VAT registration takes effect from the first taxable activity.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation. The Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is a separate legal entity and a mandatory corporate taxpayer under Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014). The standard headline corporate income tax rate is 25%, with a reduced 15% rate available for the first two taxable periods that yield a positive tax base for newly created entities (Art. 29.1 Ley 27/2014) — conditionally applicable to the MCN agency if the integrating partners did not previously carry the same activity through other entities. Territorial scope is worldwide: all income of the SL, wherever earned, is includable in the basis of assessment (Art. 7), subject to foreign tax credits, double-taxation treaties, and the participation exemption (95%/100% for qualifying foreign dividends and capital gains). No pass-through or flow-through treatment is available to the SL or its shareholders; the entity is not disregarded for Spanish purposes. Foreign shareholders are taxed only upon distribution (default 19% withholding on dividends) and must not be attributed the SL's foreign income. — For the newly incorporated SL with non-resident shareholders: (1) Before deed execution, the promoters apply for a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) by filing Form 036 (Declaración Censal) at the local AEAT office, either in person or through the notary; the intended legal representative is named as the contact person. (2) Execute the public deed of incorporation before a Spanish notary and, within the legal term, inscribe the SL in the provincial Registro Mercantil. (3) After the Mercantile Registry certificate of inscription is issued, file a second Form 036 to convert the provisional NIF into the definitive NIF; AEAT issues the definitive NIF certificate electronically. (4) Simultaneously register the economic activity (IAE epigraph Group 731 – Advertising/Publicidad if applicable) and, if any physical merchandise export will occur, apply for the Código EORI, which is linked to the definitive NIF and issued by the AEAT customs office. (5) Configure the AEAT digital certificate (certificado electrónico) and Cl@ve PIN for the legal representative to make all recurring filings (VAT Models 303/390; Corporate Income Tax Model 200; withholding Models 111, 115, 123). (6) Where a non-EU shareholder holds 10% or more, complete the statistical registration with the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores (Law 19/2003 and Law 18/2022); this is not a tax precondition but a completeness requirement. No additional tax license or pre-clearance is required to start operations; VAT registration takes effect from the first taxable activity.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation. The Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is a separate legal entity and a mandatory corporate taxpayer under Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014). The standard headline corporate income tax rate is 25%, with a reduced 15% rate available for the first two taxable periods that yield a positive tax base for newly created entities (Art. 29.1 Ley 27/2014) — conditionally applicable to the MCN agency if the integrating partners did not previously carry the same activity through other entities. Territorial scope is worldwide: all income of the SL, wherever earned, is includable in the basis of assessment (Art. 7), subject to foreign tax credits, double-taxation treaties, and the participation exemption (95%/100% for qualifying foreign dividends and capital gains). No pass-through or flow-through treatment is available to the SL or its shareholders; the entity is not disregarded for Spanish purposes. Foreign shareholders are taxed only upon distribution (default 19% withholding on dividends) and must not be attributed the SL's foreign income.

Available election forms

Spain has no check-the-box election; limited-liability entity classification is fixed under corporate law and cannot be overridden. Available elections and permanent levers relevant to the global MCN structure include: (i) Tax consolidation election (Grupo de Consolidación Fiscal, Art. 64 Ley 27/2014) available where the SL holds at least 75% of another Spanish/EU entity; jointly elected for 3 years. (ii) Participation exemption (Art. 21) is the default statutory method for qualifying foreign dividend/capital-gain income; no election is required if the minimum holding and holding-period tests are met, but the taxpayer must document the 85% foreign-tax-burden requirement and may choose the credit method via subsequent annual filings. (iii) Patent Box (Art. 23 Ley 27/2014): for own-developed software, creator-analytics platforms, or monetization technologies, a 60% reduction of qualifying net revenues (after 30% outsourcing limit) is available; requires an asset-tracking file and formal election in Model 200. (iv) REDEME election (Registro de Devolución Mensual): an exporter/adviser can opt into monthly VAT refunds by filing written declaration (Model 036) and then fully complying with SII electronic reporting; this accelerates cash refunds on input VAT. (v) Hybrid mismatch rules (ATAD II, Art. 15 bis) are mechanical, not elective; the SL should structure TikTok Creator Payout and Wise B2B payment rails to avoid payment-timing differences that could create a hybrid instrument, but no filing is available to neutralize the mismatch other than realigning the instrument within 2 years of identification. No foreign-entity reclassification (such as a REIT/regulated status) is available to an SL absent special legislation.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general de minimis threshold exists for a Spanish-established SL: any person or entity carrying on economic activity must register for IVA before commencing operations (Art. 4 Ley 37/1992). The €10,000 intra-EU distance-sales threshold is not applicable to resident taxable persons; the SL is fully VAT-registered from day one regardless of turnover. The EU SME VAT exemption (Directive (EU) 2020/285) transposition, projected with an €85,000 turnover ceiling, had not entered into force in the common Spanish regime at the date of this dossier; the full-registration rule therefore governs. Registration is effectuated through Form 036/037, updated as activity changes; no registration fee is charged; input VAT deduction rights commence from registration.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Two substantive legs: (A) Goods (creator merchandise, promotional materials): Article 21.1º Ley 37/1992 zero-rates exports of tangible goods dispatched/transported to a third country (outside the EU). To claim the 0% IVA rate, the SL must establish that the goods physically left EU customs territory—generally within 90 days from dispatch—and hold a customs export declaration (DUA/Movement Reference Number) plus transport evidence. Input VAT on all related purchases is fully deductible. (B) Services (creator representation, talent management, MCN fees, analytics, licensing, platform monétisation services supplied to TikTok group entities or to foreign creators): under the general B2B place-of-supply rule (Art. 70.Uno.1º), services rendered to a taxable person established in a non-EU country (Latin America or the United States) or in another EU Member State are located outside Spain; the SL issues the invoice without Spanish IVA (outside the scope; equivalent to zero-rating). For B2C services to consumers resident outside the EU (individual foreign creators under Art. 69), the supply is also outside the Spanish territory if the customer's habitual residence is abroad; for B2C consumers in other EU countries, the OSS scheme may cover the supply. Substantiation conditions: obtain the counterpart's valid VAT/TIN or residence certificate; execute contracts documenting the cross-border nature; maintain payment evidence (TikTok Creator Payout records, Wise B2B statements) linked to the contracts. The use-and-enjoyment exception (Art. 70.Tres) must be reviewed for applications where a foreign legal entity engages the SL for services whose effective use and enjoyment is in Spanish territory (e.g., certain electronic services and IP exploitation); proper analysis is required to confirm no re-attraction to Spain.

  • Documento Único Administrativo (DUA) / Export Declaration in the Aduana system, including the MRN (Movement Reference Number), correct EORI/NIF of the exporting SL, and the statistical value
  • Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB) or CMR carrier document, evidencing physical exit from the EU territory, together with the certificate from the office of exit (including the A/R circuit results)
  • Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank/payment-service statements (SWIFT, SEPA, Wise B2B transfers, TikTok Creator Payout logs) proving the commercial reality and receipt of consideration from the foreign counterparty — although not a legal condition for exemption, AEAT routinely requests it to substantiate the export and to prevent artificial paper-only transactions

Spain does not require per-invoice real-time fiscal clearance (no fiscal stamp analogous to the Italian SDI). The mandate is layered: (i) SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) is mandatory for VAT-payers with annual turnover exceeding €6,000,000, members of VAT groups, and those opting into REDEME; all invoice issue/receipt records must be transmitted to AEAT through web-service APIs (SOAP with X.509 digital certificate) by the fourth calendar day following the transaction, and the SII data mirror the periodic VAT return boxes. (ii) Under Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) and R.D. 1007/2023 (Verifactu), all Spanish businesses must ultimately issue electronic invoices in B2B transactions; the SL's invoicing software must generate the Facturae/XML structure with a unique Verifactu hash (based on SHA-256) and a QR stamp; records are held in the machine environment and must be formatted for AEAT access upon demand, with implementation phased by size of enterprise (phase 2 applies to an SME SL within two years of the Regulation's operational date). (iii) For customs, the electronic DUA is processed through the S.ADUANA.CW risk-management system; no tax stamp is applied to the invoice. Sanctions for non-compliant software or lack of electronic traceability range from €150 to €6,000 per offense under the LGT sanction regime (Art. 201).

AEAT applies heightened scrutiny to export zero-rating claims in the digital/agency sector, particularly where counterparties are in Latin America or use non-bank rails. The audit will verify: correct application of the B2B place-of-supply rule (a mere foreign TIN is not sufficient), the genuineness of the offshore customer relationship, and the 90-day physical-exit rule for goods. Where the exemption is incorrectly applied or substantiation fails: (i) AEAT issues a retroactive assessment charging 21% Spanish VAT on the entire invoice base; (ii) a penalty under Ley 58/2003 (LGT) applies at 50%–150% of the unpaid tax — 50% for negligent infractions and 100%–150% where false documents or intent are proven; (iii) late-payment interest (currently 3.75% per annum) runs from the original filing deadline; (iv) retrospective clawback covers the statutory 4-year limitation period (Art. 66 LGT), extended to 6 years where manipulation or hidden transactions are found; (v) in aggravated cases the criminal defraudation threshold of €120,000 (Art. 305 Código Penal) exposes the legal representative and director to 1–5 years imprisonment, fines under Art. 310 bis, and mandatory restitution; (vi) customs AEO status and future customs simplifications may be withdrawn. Prevention: maintain contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation (Chapter V OECD TP Guidelines) that aligns intercompany fees with the creator-payout logic, perform annual validation of counterparties' TIN status, and preserve the entire export file for at least 6 years.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Full convertibility applies to both current-account and capital-account transactions because Spain is a euro-area member with no exchange-control approval regime. Profit remittance and dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are not subject to FX licensing; they only trigger the 19% IRNR (Non-Resident Income Tax) withholding and, above the statutory threshold, an ex-post statistical declaration to Banco de España. The practical hurdles for an ES_SL are therefore documentary, not regulatory: (i) dividends require audited annual accounts and a notarial shareholders' resolution; and (ii) foreign direct investment into Spain and outbound payments above €100,000 per transaction (or a cumulative €1,000,000 in one natural year) must be reported through the D1-1 / D2 statistical declarations (under Royal Decree 664/1999 and Banco de España Circular 4/2017). No prior authorization is required for these flows.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain imposes no mandatory surrender requirement, no forced conversion ratio, and no statutory timeline for repatriation of export or service-proceeds. The ES_SL may lawfully retain creator and advertising income in USD (or other currencies) in a 'cuenta en divisas' held with a Spanish bank, or convert to EUR at market rate at any time. However, every receipt from non-resident payers exceeding €100,000 must be reported to Banco de España under the monthly statistical model D-2; the bank shall record the 'posición de divisas' for the corporate client. The only de-facto RL constraint is that the company must be able to evidence the commercial origin of the proceeds to the AML department.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) is the national central bank and payment-systems supervisor; the European Central Bank (ECB) governs euro-area monetary policy. Foreign-exchange and capital-movement oversight for non-resident operations is jointly executed by Banco de España (statistical collection, AML supervision, payment institution licensing) and the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCIIN) within the Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa, under Ley 13/1994, Ley 10/2010 (on AML/CTF), and Royal Decree 664/1999 (regulating foreign transactions and capital movements).

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Wise Fit: High

Feasibility: High as a supplementary treasury rail, Low as the primary banking relationship. An EEA-licensed e-money institution (EMI) such as Wise Europe SA (licensed by the National Bank of Belgium and passporting into Spain under PSD2/EMD2) is legally accepted in Spain through its registration with Banco de España and may be used for B2B creator payouts and international settlements, including the target Wise_B2B rail. Critical constraints: (i) an EMI account cannot grant overdraft or credit, so it cannot replace the main operational account at a credit institution; (ii) the ES_SL must keep its tax-related bank account in Spain for NIF registration and VAT refunds; (iii) the EMI must produce a traceable audit trail acceptable to SEPBLAC if creator payouts exceed €10,000,000/annum; (iv) non-EEA offshore EMIs (unlicensed UK-only or Caribbean/Asia-licensed entities) are not viable as principal settlement rail and would expose the SL to regulatory non-compliance; and (v) incoming capital contributions into an ES_SL may only be received on a Spanish IBAN belonging to the corporate entity itself, so the EMI is best used only for outbound disbursement liquidity.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Capital injection from a non-EU holding company or from a platform treasury (e.g., TikTok Ireland / TikTok Singapore) referencing 'royalties' or 'creator commission' without supporting documents, triggering source-of-funds suspicion.

Root cause: Capital injection from a non-EU holding company or from a platform treasury (e.g., TikTok Ireland / TikTok Singapore) referencing 'royalties' or 'creator commission' without supporting documents, triggering source-of-funds suspicion.

Defense evidence: The signed global platform partnership agreement (MCN contract) showing commission mechanics; the pre-incorporation pro-forma invoice and corresponding platform payout ledger; the intercompany service or capital-contribution agreement; audited or notarised bank statements of the sending entity for the last 12 months; certificate of incorporation of the sending entity, apostilled and translated; and a written 'carta de declaración de negocio' signed by the SL's administrator explaining the commercial purpose and expected monthly volume.
Beneficial-ownership chain located in high-risk or non-EU jurisdictions (e.g., ultimate individual shareholder resident in Latin America or offshore jurisdictions), triggering 'high-risk PEP / tax-haven' scoring.

Root cause: Beneficial-ownership chain located in high-risk or non-EU jurisdictions (e.g., ultimate individual shareholder resident in Latin America or offshore jurisdictions), triggering 'high-risk PEP / tax-haven' scoring.

Defense evidence: Certificado de titularidad real signed by the SL secretary; the Libro Registro de Socios (shareholder ledger) stamped by the notary; the full escritura listing shareholders and the share-capital structure; apostilled and legalised identity documents and residential tax-certificates of all direct and indirect shareholders; a shareholder-source-of-wealth letter with supporting bank/investment statements; and (if an ultimate parent exists) its consolidated group structure chart.
High-frequency outbound payments to Latin American creators (e.g., weekly payouts to Argentina, Brazil, Mexico, Chile) falsely profiled under the 'structuring' or 'fraud-mule' detection engines.

Root cause: High-frequency outbound payments to Latin American creators (e.g., weekly payouts to Argentina, Brazil, Mexico, Chile) falsely profiled under the 'structuring' or 'fraud-mule' detection engines.

Defense evidence: A centralised creator KYC file per creator (passport, signed sub-agency representation agreement, creator platform ID and social-media handle, country tax ID); the monthly platform payout reconciliation ledger signed by the administrator; an internal AML/CTF manual (even a simplified one-page procedural policy) appointing a compliance contact; and a clear payment-schedule invoice series matching the SL's declared ISIC 7310 activity.
FX treasury transactions mixing EUR inflows with USD outflows to creators and to the parent/holding company, triggering the bank's exchange transaction and capital-confusion alerts.

Root cause: FX treasury transactions mixing EUR inflows with USD outflows to creators and to the parent/holding company, triggering the bank's exchange transaction and capital-confusion alerts.

Defense evidence: A board resolution of the SL approving an annual FX hedging policy; the weekly foreign-currency position and exposure report; confirming deals (FX spot/forward tickets) from the principal commercial bank; the monthly reconciliation between creator invoices, platform settlements, and treasury conversions; and, where derivatives are used, a signed CMOF (Contrato Marco de Operaciones Financieras) or ISDA master agreement.
Sanctions-screening hit: a creator, shareholder, or beneficiary appears on the EU consolidated sanctions list, CAAS/OFAC lists, or the Spanish 'Lista de Orden' (e.g., due to Russian/Ukrainian exposure or sanctioned LATAM nationals), causing account freeze.

Root cause: Sanctions-screening hit: a creator, shareholder, or beneficiary appears on the EU consolidated sanctions list, CAAS/OFAC lists, or the Spanish 'Lista de Orden' (e.g., due to Russian/Ukrainian exposure or sanctioned LATAM nationals), causing account freeze.

Defense evidence: A professional sanctions and PEP clearance report prepared before account opening, covering all shareholders, directors, beneficial owners, and the full creator roster against the European Commission consolidated list and United Nations Security Council list; the signed sworn declaration by the administrator confirming no blocked individual has any entitlement; and a post-hit remediation letter explaining the legal basis for un-freezing (usually a false-positive with an explanatory passport/address match) — the bank typically releases funds within 10 business days after a complete dossier submission.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

The compliant inbound path for an ES_SL receiving foreign capital is via SWIFT wire to the SL's capital escrow or operational EUR account held at a Tier-1 Spanish bank. The remitter must send the SWIFT MT103 payment with the following mandatory elements: field 50F (ordering party), field 59 (beneficiary ES_SL IBAN, format ES00 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000), field 70 with the narrative 'INVERSION DIRECTA / APORTACION DE CAPITAL / SL [TAX ID NIF] / [NOTARY PROTOCOL NUMBER & DATE]', and field 71A (OUR charges). The corresponding statistical obligation is the D1-1 declaration to Banco de España for foreign direct investment above €100,000, filed within the month following the operation; the bank will request the share-issue certificate and the notarial escritura of capital contribution before releasing funds for operational use. Fund availability should be planned with a minimum of 5 business days for verification; where the remitter is the ultimate shareholder, additional proof of source of funds (shareholder bank statements, tax filings, structure chart) must be pre-delivered to the account manager to avoid 72-hour suspension under AML investigations.The ES_SL MCN agency will use three main clearing rails: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT, IBAN-to-IBAN) for all EU/EEA creators and partners — no FX exposure, settlement T+1, with SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for sub-€100,000 payouts requiring T0 settlement and 10-second finality; (ii) SWIFT MT103 (with correspondent bank details for non-SEPA destinations, e.g., UK, USA, Brazil, Mexico, Argentina) for creator payouts in local currency or USD, attaching the invoice reference in field 70 and using 'OUR' charges; and (iii) optionally, a Commercial Letter of Credit (crédito documentario) — although this is only commercially justified for advertising or content-production purchase flows requiring shipping/performance documents; for pure creator royalties and MCN commissions, LCs are legally possible but operationally inefficient and therefore not recommended. Every outbound payment exceeding €100,000 must be declared to Banco de España under model D2, and a quarterly 'declaración de posición de divisas' should reconcile the USD treasury account. For USD-denominated creator payouts routed via Latin America, the SL should also consider the use of local payment-rail aggregators (via the EMI rail) to reduce FX spreads, but the main bank remains the sole settlement institution for amounts above the EMI's concentration threshold.FX Spot (EUR/USD and T2 currency pairs) executed with the main Spanish commercial bank at market rate, without any derivative wrapper or pre-approval requirement, used for weekly creator-payout conversions.Outright FX Forward (compraventa a plazo) with tenors up to 12 months for EUR/USD, permissible under the Spanish CMOF (Contrato Marco de Operaciones Financieras) framework, allowing the SL to lock the monthly creator-payout conversion rate; no Banco de España approval is required for hedging contracts with an authorised credit institution.FX Swap (compraventa de divisas combinada/segunda operación) with tenors from 1 week to 6 months, used to fund the USD operational account without leaving an open overnight FX position; documented under the same CMOF framework.Cross-Currency Swap (CCS) for 1–3 year hedging ladders (e.g., converting a USD-denominated platform treasury stream into EUR), documented under ISDA and CMOF, subject to the bank's counterparty credit limits and EMIR clearing obligations.FX Options (EUR/USD calls and puts) purchased OTC from the principal Spanish bank, permissible under MiFID II when the bank acts as governed dealer; premiums paid in EUR; the SL must show that it is acting for hedging motives (its corporate-object clause will generally prohibit speculative net-open positions).Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are NOT permissible or economically valid for EUR/USD because the pair is fully deliverable in the EU; NDFs may only be lawfully applied to exotic, non-convertible, or restricted-deliverability currencies (e.g., certain LATAM/APAC local currencies) and must be separately documented under an ISDA 1998 NDF Master Agreement with an appropriately licensed credit institution; without that structure, any NDF would be treated as a speculative over-the-counter derivative and would exceed the SL's permitted treasury mandate.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility: High as a supplementary treasury rail, Low as the primary banking relationship. An EEA-licensed e-money institution (EMI) such as Wise Europe SA (licensed by the National Bank of Belgium and passporting into Spain under PSD2/EMD2) is legally accepted in Spain through its registration with Banco de España and may be used for B2B creator payouts and international settlements, including the target Wise_B2B rail. Critical constraints: (i) an EMI account cannot grant overdraft or credit, so it cannot replace the main operational account at a credit institution; (ii) the ES_SL must keep its tax-related bank account in Spain for NIF registration and VAT refunds; (iii) the EMI must produce a traceable audit trail acceptable to SEPBLAC if creator payouts exceed €10,000,000/annum; (iv) non-EEA offshore EMIs (unlicensed UK-only or Caribbean/Asia-licensed entities) are not viable as principal settlement rail and would expose the SL to regulatory non-compliance; and (v) incoming capital contributions into an ES_SL may only be received on a Spanish IBAN belonging to the corporate entity itself, so the EMI is best used only for outbound disbursement liquidity.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: EUR 50,000,000 consolidated group turnover for Master File/Local File

Economic substance scope: Spain enforces ESR for preferential regimes and holding entities, requiring genuine local economic activities

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax return non-filing or late submission

Statutory sanction: Fines €1,500-€3,000 plus daily €10-€20 surcharges; criminal prosecution possible

Director personal liability: Personal restitution, fines, and imprisonment for fraudulent non-filing
Transfer pricing non-compliance

Statutory sanction: Tax adjustments, penalties up to 100% of additional tax, and interest charges

Director personal liability: Joint and several liability, potential management disqualification
Dividend WHT evasion or under-withholding

Statutory sanction: Administrative fines and criminal tax evasion charges (up to 50% of evaded tax)

Director personal liability: Imprisonment, travel bans, and personal payment of taxes plus surcharges
Economic substance and TP abuse

Statutory sanction: Denial of tax benefits, back taxes, penalties, and criminal sanctions

Director personal liability: Personal liability including imprisonment and disqualification
